SNR tutorial

The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) can be calculated using the function SNR. Its inputs are the waveform model, the source parameters, and the detector network. The output is the total network SNR.

SNR[Appr, fp, {det1, det2, ...}]

Calculates the SNR for the waveform model Appr, with source parameters fp, and the detector network {det1, det2, ...}.

Parameters

  • Appr: Waveform model. Supported values are "IMRPhenomD" and "IMRPhenomHM".

  • fp: Association containing the source parameters.

  • {det1, det2, ...}: List of associations representing the detectors in the network.

Returns

The total SNR of the detector network.

The convention for fp follows section Fiducial point and the convention for deti follows section Detector association.

Example

The following example calculates the SNR using the IMRPhenomD waveform model:

fp = <|
    "dec" -> 3.14/2, "phi" -> 3.4, "psi" -> 0.1,
    "Mc" -> 0.0116, "q" -> 0.2,
    "s1z" -> 0.1, "s2z" -> 0.1, "iota" -> 2.5,
    "invdL" -> 1, "tc" -> 10, "phiRef" -> 0.
|>;

H1 = <|
    "Position" -> DetectorVertex["H1"],
    "DetectorTensor" -> DetectorTensor["H1"],
    "ASD" -> ASD["L1H1-O5"]
|>;

L1 = <|
    "Position" -> DetectorVertex["L1"],
    "DetectorTensor" -> DetectorTensor["L1"],
    "ASD" -> ASD["L1H1-O5"]
|>;

snr = SNR["IMRPhenomD", fp, {H1, L1}];

Options

The function also accepts options to specify the frequency range, resolution and whether to return the SNR of each detector separately. The default settings are shown below:

snr = SNR[
    "IMRPhenomD", fp, {H1, L1},
    "fmin" -> 10, "fmax" -> 1024,
    "res" -> 1000, "AllSNRs" -> False
]

When "AllSNRs" -> True the function returns a list containing the SNR of each detector in the network. The order of SNRs is the same of the detector network, in this case {H1, L1}.
